articles.title: BPL card eligibility set for major change? Karnataka plans to raise income limit from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹3 lakh
articles.description: The Karnataka government is considering increasing the annual income limit for BPL card eligibility from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹3 lakh. The proposal, based on the Administrative Reforms Commission's recommendation, could bring more families under the welfare system if approved by the Cabinet. Thousands of families in Karnataka could soon become eligible for Below Poverty Line (BPL) benefits as the State government is considering a major revision to the annual income ceiling for BPL card eligibility. Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister K.H. Muniyappa has said the government is planning to increase the existing income limit from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹3 lakh, following the recommendations of the Administrative Reforms Commission. The proposal was discussed during a review meeting of the State's guarantee schemes, jointly chaired by Minister K.H. Muniyappa and Karnataka State Guarantee Schemes Implementation Committee Chairman H.M. Revanna. According to the Minister, the move is intended to extend government welfare benefits to more deserving families. He also said he plans to place the proposal before the State Cabinet in the coming days. The recommendation to increase the income ceiling was made by the Administrative Reforms Commission. Several organisations had also urged the government to revise the limit, stating that the current income cap no longer reflects the financial realities of many families. The government is now examining both the benefits and challenges of implementing the proposal. If everything proceeds as planned, the revised income limit could be announced soon. Also Read: Big Relief for Anna Bhagya beneficiaries: Karnataka extends ration shop timings from 6 AM to 10 PM If the income ceiling is increased to ₹3 lakh, the number of BPL card holders in Karnataka is expected to rise significantly. Many families currently covered under the Above Poverty Line (APL) category could become eligible to apply for BPL cards. At the same time, officials are also aware that a larger beneficiary base could make the distribution of subsidised food grains and other welfare benefits more challenging. At present, Karnataka has around 1.20 crore BPL card holders. In recent months, the government carried out a verification drive after concerns that many ineligible people had obtained BPL cards. During the exercise, BPL cards held by income tax payers and other ineligible beneficiaries were cancelled. Reports indicated that nearly 3 to 4 lakh cards were found to be ineligible and were withdrawn. The proposal to raise the income limit comes after this verification process. Apart from the proposed income limit revision, the Food Department is also preparing to roll out the Indira Food Kit under the Anna Bhagya scheme within the next two to three months. Muniyappa said the tender process, estimated to cost around ₹6,000 crore, is in its final stage. The project has taken time because of its large scale and the need for detailed scrutiny. The objective of the food kit is to encourage people to consume more nutritious food along with rice. The Minister also provided an update on the Anna Suvidha scheme, which delivers ration to the doorsteps of elderly and vulnerable beneficiaries. Also Read: No rain, rising prices: Monsoon failure pushes grocery costs higher, farmers and families under pressure The government has also revised the distribution pattern under the Anna Bhagya scheme, which benefits 4.42 crore people across Karnataka. Beneficiaries will now receive 10 kg of food grains, comprising 7 kg of rice and 3 kg of ragi. Of the rice supplied, 5 kg is provided by the State government, while the Central government contributes 2 kg of rice and 3 kg of ragi. To support the revised food distribution, Karnataka has procured 5.60 lakh metric tonnes of ragi under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) scheme. The stock is currently being processed for distribution. Recognising different food habits across regions, the government has also made a special arrangement for North Karnataka. Since ragi consumption is relatively low there and sufficient jowar could not be procured under the MSP scheme, beneficiaries in the region will receive 8 kg of rice and 2 kg of jowar instead of 7 kg of rice and 3 kg of ragi. To improve public access to ration supplies, officials have been instructed to keep all 20,259 fair price shops across Karnataka open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day. Beneficiaries facing any issues can register complaints through the department's toll-free Anna Helpline (1967). Also Read: Instagram DM calling classmate 'Pretty' is not a crime, rules Karnataka High Court The government is also considering displaying photographs and contact details of the Chief Minister, Deputy Chief Minister, Ministers and the Chairman of the Guarantee Schemes Implementation Committee at all fair price shops. Meanwhile, the department is strengthening monitoring systems to prevent the diversion of Public Distribution System (PDS) food grains into the black market. A new command and control centre is being established at the department headquarters. CCTV cameras have already been installed in government warehouses, while GPS tracking devices have been fitted to vehicles transporting ration supplies. Muniyappa also said the Legal Metrology Department has collected nearly ₹90 crore in penalties during the current financial year for violations such as cheating consumers through incorrect weights and measures. The amount is expected to cross ₹100 crore before the end of the financial year. The proposed increase in the BPL income limit is now under active consideration. If approved by the Cabinet, it could become one of the biggest changes to Karnataka's welfare eligibility criteria in recent years, expanding access to government benefits while also increasing the responsibility of ensuring that only genuinely eligible families receive support.

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Rollout Begins in West Bengal Following State Committee Formation
articles.description: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Rollout Begins in West Bengal Following State Committee Formation New Delhi, Jul 24 (KNN) The Ministry of MSME has begun implementing the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in West Bengal following the constitution of the State Monitoring Committee and District Implementation Committees by the West Bengal Government on May 14, 2026. The information was provided by Union Minister of State for MSME Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. PM Vishwakarma was launched on September 17, 2023, to provide end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades, including carpentry, pottery, goldsmithing, tailoring, masonry and fishing net making. Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), 5.82 crore loans amounting to Rs 3.55 lakh crore have been disbursed in West Bengal from April 8, 2015, to June 26, 2026. The Ministry has also stated that 23 Host Institutes are operating in West Bengal under the Incubation Component of the MSME Innovative Scheme. Each approved idea is eligible for financial support of up to Rs 15 lakh. Women entrepreneurs, including those based in the Sundarbans, are eligible for support under various schemes, including Udyam Registration, the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, CGTMSE, PMEGP, PM Vishwakarma, the Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme and the Yashasvini Campaign. (KNN Bureau)

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma and PMMY Boost MSMEs in West Bengal
articles.description: PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17.09.2023 to provide end-to-end holistic support to artisans and craftspeople of 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tools. The scheme covers 18 trades, namely Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal Artisan, Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear Artisan, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor and Fishing Net Maker. The implementation of PM Vishwakarma has commenced in the State of West Bengal following the issuance of a notification by the Government of West Bengal constituting the State Monitoring Committee and District Implementation Committees on 14.05.2026 for the roll-out of the Scheme in the State. Under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), a total of 5.82 crore loans amounting to Rs. 3.55 lakh crore have been disbursed since inception i.e. 08.04.2015 till 26.06.2026 in the State of West Bengal. The Government has undertaken the following initiatives for potential women beneficiaries throughout the country including Sundarbans-based women entrepreneurs and fisherfolk: Udyam Registration Portal (UR) and Udyam Assist Portal (UAP): women owned enterprises registered are eligible to avail benefits under various schemes of the Ministry including access to Priority Sector Lending. Public Procurement Policy for MSEs: Central Ministries and CPSEs are mandated to procure atleast 3% of their annual procurement from women owned Micro and Small Enterprises, thereby facilitating market access. Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE): women owned Micro and Small Enterprises are eligible for enhanced guarantee coverage of upto 90% (as against 75% for others) and a 10% concession in the annual guarantee fee. PMEGP: Women beneficiaries are categorized under Special Category and eligible for a higher Margin Money (MM) Subsidy rate of upto 35% and lower own contribution of 5% of project cost, compared to 25% MM Subsidy rate and 10% own contribution of project cost for beneficiaries under General category. Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana: Women artisans engaged in the coir sector are provided with skill upgradation training under the Coir Vikas Yojana to enhance their employability and entrepreneurial capabilities. Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme: women entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance of upto 100% of the admissible expenditure for participation in domestic trade fairs, compared to 80% for other entrepreneurs. PM Vishwakarma Scheme: women artisans engaged in any of the 18 notified trades are eligible for benefits including skill training, toolkit incentive, collateral free credit support, incentive for digital transactions and marketing support. Yashasvini Campaign: Ministry undertakes awareness, handholding, mentorship and capacity building activities to facilitate access of existing and aspiring women entrepreneurs to various Government schemes and institutional support. The Incubation Component of the MSME Innovative Scheme of the Ministry of MSME is aimed at promoting innovation, support new ideas, and facilitate the transformation of concepts into viable business ventures. It plays a crucial role in strengthening the MSME and thus, start-up ecosystem by nurturing early-stage ideas. It supports the process of incubation through Host Institutes (HI), which are academic institutions and Innovation centers acting as Business Incubators (BI) across the country. Currently, there are 23 Host Institutes (HI) in West Bengal and each approved idea is eligible for financial support of up to a maximum amount of Rs. 15 lakh.
